description: Running the defensive side of security: the security operations centre, logging and log analysis, intrusion detection, threat intelligence, the incident response life cycle, containment and recovery, and the lessons-learned and reporting that close an incident. Taught through browser-based simulations of a monitored network and a live incident, where students triage alerts, investigate logs and work a response on isolated virtual machines.
modelledOn: Sanders and Smith, Applied Network Security Monitoring
NIST SP 800-61 Computer Security Incident Handling Guide
outcomes: Describe how a security operations centre is staffed, tiered and measured.
Collect, normalise and analyse logs to detect and investigate suspicious activity.
Deploy and tune intrusion detection and correlate alerts in a SIEM.
Use threat intelligence and the ATT&CK framework to prioritise detection and hunting.
Work an incident through the full life cycle from detection to recovery.
Conduct a post-incident review and write reports for technical and management audiences.

units.title: Security operations centres
topics: The mission of a SOC: monitor, detect, triage, respond and improve
Tiered analyst roles, shift handover and escalation paths
Metrics that matter: dwell time, mean time to detect and respond, false-positive rate
People, process and technology; build-versus-outsource for a small Ghanaian bank or university
The monitored-network simulation and the analyst's console

units.title: Logging and log analysis
topics: Log sources: endpoints, servers, network devices, applications, cloud and authentication systems
Collection, time synchronisation, normalisation and retention; log integrity and tamper resistance
Searching and pivoting through logs to reconstruct a sequence of events
Baselining normal behaviour to make anomalies visible, including on shared internet-cafe machines
Parsing a mobile-money fraud attempt from authentication and transaction logs

units.title: Intrusion detection
topics: Host and network intrusion detection and prevention; signature versus anomaly detection
Writing and tuning rules with Snort and Suricata; reducing noise
Network security monitoring with Zeek and endpoint telemetry with an EDR agent
Detecting scans, exploitation and command-and-control traffic in the simulator
False positives, false negatives and the cost of each

units.title: SIEM and correlation
topics: Aggregating sources into a SIEM; parsing, enrichment and correlation rules
Dashboards, alerting and case management
Detection engineering: turning an attack technique into a reliable detection
Mapping detections to MITRE ATT&CK for coverage
Managing alert fatigue and prioritisation

units.title: Threat intelligence
topics: Strategic, operational and tactical threat intelligence and who consumes each
Indicators of compromise, the pyramid of pain and the limits of indicators
Sharing and standards: STIX, TAXII and community feeds relevant to West Africa
Threat hunting hypotheses driven by ATT&CK techniques
Attribution, bias and avoiding over-reading an indicator

units.title: The incident response life cycle
topics: The phases: preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned
Preparation: the incident response plan, roles, the RACI, communications and legal contacts
Classifying and prioritising incidents by impact and urgency
Evidence handling and chain of custody for a possible prosecution under the Cybersecurity Act 2020
Declaring an incident and standing up the response team in the simulation

units.title: Containment and recovery
topics: Short-term and long-term containment; isolating hosts without destroying evidence
Eradication: removing malware, closing the entry vector, resetting credentials
Digital forensics basics: disk and memory acquisition, timeline building
Recovery: restoring from clean backups, validating integrity and monitoring for recurrence
Working an incident through brown-outs and unreliable power with offline runbooks

units.title: Lessons learned and reporting
topics: The post-incident review: what happened, what worked, what to change, without blame
Root-cause analysis and tracking remediation to completion
Reporting to management and to the regulator or affected customers
Feeding lessons back into detections, playbooks and training
Updating runbooks and the response plan

units.title: Running a full response exercise
topics: A tabletop and a live simulated breach combining detection, triage and response
Coordinating containment, communication and recovery under time pressure
Producing the incident report and the improvement plan
Capstone: lead the response to a simulated ransomware outbreak and present the after-action review

schedule.title: The SOC mission and metrics
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page brief explaining dwell time, mean time to detect and mean time to respond to a manager who has never seen them before.

tasks.title: Match five SOC activities (monitor, detect, triage, respond, improve) to the stage of the mission they belong to, for a described alert
Decide which tier of analyst should handle three described alerts, and explain what should trigger an escalation to the next tier
Compute dwell time and mean time to respond from a timeline of a described incident, and judge whether the SOC met its target

schedule.title: People, process, technology and the console
schedule.exercise: Write a short recommendation on build-versus-outsource for a small Ghanaian bank's SOC, weighing cost, skills and coverage.

tasks.title: Weigh build-versus-outsource for a described small organisation's SOC across people, process and technology, and justify a recommendation
Open the monitored-network simulation and the analyst console, and locate where alerts, logs and host status are each shown
Walk through the analyst console for a described quiet shift and identify which of ten log entries is worth a closer look, with reasons

schedule.title: Log sources and searching
schedule.exercise: Write a checklist of the log sources a SOC needs to reconstruct a login followed by a suspicious file access, and why each source matters.

tasks.title: List the log sources (endpoint, server, network device, authentication) that a described incident would touch, and what each would show
Search and pivot through a set of logs to reconstruct the order of events in a described login-then-access incident
Check a batch of logs for time synchronisation and integrity problems, and explain how an unsynchronised clock would break an investigation

schedule.title: Baselining and fraud parsing
schedule.exercise: Explain, with an example, how knowing what is normal for a shared internet-cafe machine helps an analyst spot what is not.

tasks.title: Establish a baseline of normal login times and locations for a described user, and flag the one login that breaks the pattern
Parse a set of authentication and transaction logs to find the sequence consistent with an attempted mobile-money fraud, and state the evidence
Compare baselines for two shared machines with different usage patterns, and decide which anomaly thresholds would suit each

schedule.title: Detection technologies
schedule.exercise: Explain the difference between signature and anomaly detection with one example each of a threat that only one of them would catch.

tasks.title: Decide whether five described detections came from a signature rule or anomaly detection, and explain the evidence for each
Write a detection rule for a described scan pattern, tune it against a quiet baseline, and show it no longer fires on normal traffic
Review a captured sequence of traffic for a scan, an exploitation attempt and command-and-control activity, and label which stage each log entry shows

schedule.title: SIEM, detection engineering and ATT&CK
schedule.exercise: Map three described attack techniques to MITRE ATT&CK, and identify one technique the current detection set does not cover.

tasks.title: Aggregate three log sources into a SIEM view, write a correlation rule linking two of them, and show it fires only on the intended pattern
Turn a described attack technique into a reliable detection rule, and show it fires on the technique without firing on normal activity
Map five existing detection rules to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, and identify the coverage gap that most needs a new rule

schedule.title: Threat intelligence
schedule.exercise: Explain the pyramid of pain with one indicator type at each level, and say which level is hardest for an attacker to change.

tasks.title: Decide which audience (strategic, operational, tactical) a described piece of threat intelligence serves, and what they would do with it
Rank three indicators of compromise by the pyramid of pain, and explain why the hardest one to change is the most valuable detection
Form a threat-hunting hypothesis from a described ATT&CK technique, and list the log evidence that would confirm or disprove it

schedule.title: Incident response preparation
schedule.exercise: Write the first page of an incident response plan for a small organisation, covering roles, a RACI table and communication contacts.

tasks.title: Map a described security event onto the incident response phases (preparation through lessons learned), and identify which phase is missing
Build a RACI table for a described incident response team, and resolve a case where two roles both claim ownership of a decision
Classify three described incidents by impact and urgency, and decide which should be declared a major incident

schedule.title: Evidence and declaring an incident
schedule.exercise: Write the chain-of-custody log entries you would expect for evidence collected from a compromised host, and explain why each field matters.

tasks.title: Complete a chain-of-custody log for evidence collected during a described incident, and identify the one missing entry that would weaken a prosecution
Declare a described incident, stand up the response team and assign the first three actions, scored against a response rubric
Decide what evidence handling steps a described incident needs to remain usable under the Cybersecurity Act 2020, and flag one step that was skipped

schedule.title: Containment, eradication and forensics
schedule.exercise: Write the trade-off between isolating a host immediately and leaving it running briefly to preserve volatile evidence, with a recommendation.

tasks.title: Isolate a compromised host in the simulated network without powering it off, and explain what evidence this preserves compared with disconnecting power
Remove a described malware's persistence mechanism and close its entry vector, then verify the host no longer shows signs of compromise
Build a timeline of a described incident from disk and memory evidence, and identify the first and last moments of attacker activity

schedule.title: Recovery under constraints
schedule.exercise: Write an offline runbook for restoring a service from backup during a power outage, listing every step an analyst could follow without network access.

tasks.title: Decide which of three available backups is safe to restore from after a described incident, and justify rejecting the other two
Walk through an incident response using an offline runbook during a simulated brown-out, and identify which steps would have failed without it
Validate the integrity of a restored service against a described checklist, and decide whether monitoring should continue before declaring recovery complete

schedule.title: Post-incident review and reporting
schedule.exercise: Write the after-action review structure (what happened, what worked, what to change) for a described incident, keeping it free of blame.

tasks.title: Run a blameless post-incident review for a described incident, separating contributing factors from individual blame
Track a described post-incident remediation item to completion, and decide what evidence shows it was actually fixed rather than just logged
Draft the report sections a described incident needs for management and for the regulator, and decide what detail each audience needs

schedule.title: Tabletop exercise and the capstone response
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page after-action summary for a simulated ransomware outbreak, covering detection, decisions made under pressure and the lessons for the playbook.

tasks.title: Run a tabletop exercise for a described breach scenario, deciding the first three actions each role should take in the first ten minutes
Coordinate containment, communication and recovery for a described incident under a tight deadline, and justify the order chosen
Lead the response to a simulated ransomware outbreak from detection through recovery and present the after-action review, scored on a capstone rubric
